---
id: c-kway-merge
title: K-Way Merge of Sorted Logs with a Heap
difficulty: Hard
order: 1
tags: binary heap, priority queue, merging, structs
time_limit: 2
---
## Statement
A robot fleet produces **k timestamp-sorted logs**. Merge them into one globally sorted stream using a **binary min-heap** of size k (O(N log k)). Implement the heap yourself (no `qsort` on the whole data: the driver measures nothing, but the tests are large enough that sorting everything is borderline, and a heap is the intended solution).

Input: `k`, then k logs, each `m t1 v1 t2 v2 ... tm vm` (m entries with non-decreasing timestamps `t` and integer values `v`). Then a line `Q`, followed by Q queries.

Output:
1. `merged N`, then the first 10 merged entries as `t:v (log L)`. Ties in `t` break by smaller log index, then by the original position within that log.
2. `checksum C`, where C = Σ (position_in_merged_stream × v) mod 1 000 000 007, with positions starting at 1.
3. For each query `top K`: the K largest values in the merged stream, in descending order, found with a **min-heap of size K** (not by sorting everything). For `median`: the lower median of all values, using the two-heap technique or `nth_element`-style selection.

## Starter
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(void) {
    return 0;
}
```

## Hints
- Heap items: `typedef struct { long t; int log, idx; } Item;`, compared by `(t, log, idx)`. Pop the smallest, output it, and push the next entry from the same log.
- Write `sift_up`/`sift_down` generically with a `less(const Item*, const Item*)` function.
- Top K: a min-heap of `long` values with size ≤ K. Push each value, and when the size exceeds K, pop the minimum. At the end, the heap holds the K largest: pop them all and print in reverse.
- Median: a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half, or copy the values and use quickselect.
- For the checksum, use `long long` and reduce modulo 10⁹+7 at each step. Values can be negative, so normalise with `((x % M) + M) % M`.

## Solution
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#define MOD 1000000007LL

typedef struct { long t; int log, idx; } Item;
typedef struct { long *t, *v; int n; } Log;

static int item_less(const Item *a, const Item *b) {
    if (a->t != b->t) return a->t < b->t;
    if (a->log != b->log) return a->log < b->log;
    return a->idx < b->idx;
}

static void item_sift_up(Item *h, int i) {
    while (i > 0) {
        int p = (i - 1) / 2;
        if (!item_less(&h[i], &h[p])) break;
        Item tmp = h[i]; h[i] = h[p]; h[p] = tmp;
        i = p;
    }
}

static void item_sift_down(Item *h, int n, int i) {
    for (;;) {
        int l = 2 * i + 1, r = l + 1, m = i;
        if (l < n && item_less(&h[l], &h[m])) m = l;
        if (r < n && item_less(&h[r], &h[m])) m = r;
        if (m == i) return;
        Item tmp = h[i]; h[i] = h[m]; h[m] = tmp;
        i = m;
    }
}

/* a generic long heap: sign = +1 for a min-heap, -1 for a max-heap */
static void lh_push(long *h, int *n, long v, int sign) {
    int i = (*n)++;
    h[i] = v;
    while (i > 0) {
        int p = (i - 1) / 2;
        if (sign * h[i] >= sign * h[p]) break;
        long tmp = h[i]; h[i] = h[p]; h[p] = tmp;
        i = p;
    }
}

static long lh_pop(long *h, int *n, int sign) {
    long top = h[0];
    h[0] = h[--(*n)];
    int i = 0;
    for (;;) {
        int l = 2 * i + 1, r = l + 1, m = i;
        if (l < *n && sign * h[l] < sign * h[m]) m = l;
        if (r < *n && sign * h[r] < sign * h[m]) m = r;
        if (m == i) break;
        long tmp = h[i]; h[i] = h[m]; h[m] = tmp;
        i = m;
    }
    return top;
}

int main(void) {
    int k;
    if (scanf("%d", &k) != 1) return 1;
    Log *logs = calloc((size_t)k, sizeof *logs);
    int total = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) {
        scanf("%d", &logs[i].n);
        logs[i].t = malloc(((size_t)logs[i].n + 1) * sizeof(long));
        logs[i].v = malloc(((size_t)logs[i].n + 1) * sizeof(long));
        for (int j = 0; j < logs[i].n; j++) scanf("%ld %ld", &logs[i].t[j], &logs[i].v[j]);
        total += logs[i].n;
    }

    Item *heap = malloc(((size_t)k + 1) * sizeof *heap);
    int hn = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < k; i++)
        if (logs[i].n > 0) { heap[hn] = (Item){logs[i].t[0], i, 0}; item_sift_up(heap, hn++); }

    long *merged_v = malloc(((size_t)total + 1) * sizeof(long));
    long long checksum = 0;
    int pos = 0;
    printf("merged %d\n", total);
    while (hn > 0) {
        Item top = heap[0];
        long v = logs[top.log].v[top.idx];
        if (pos < 10) printf("%ld:%ld (log %d)\n", top.t, v, top.log);
        merged_v[pos++] = v;
        checksum = (checksum + (long long)pos % MOD * (((v % MOD) + MOD) % MOD)) % MOD;
        if (top.idx + 1 < logs[top.log].n) {                     /* replace the root with the log's next entry */
            heap[0] = (Item){logs[top.log].t[top.idx + 1], top.log, top.idx + 1};
        } else {
            heap[0] = heap[--hn];
        }
        item_sift_down(heap, hn, 0);
    }
    printf("checksum %lld\n", checksum);

    int q;
    scanf("%d", &q);
    long *h1 = malloc(((size_t)total + 1) * sizeof(long)), *h2 = malloc(((size_t)total + 1) * sizeof(long));
    char cmd[16];
    while (q-- > 0 && scanf("%15s", cmd) == 1) {
        if (strcmp(cmd, "top") == 0) {
            int K, n = 0;
            scanf("%d", &K);
            for (int i = 0; i < total; i++) {
                lh_push(h1, &n, merged_v[i], 1);
                if (n > K) lh_pop(h1, &n, 1);                       /* drop the smallest */
            }
            int cnt = n;
            for (int i = cnt - 1; i >= 0; i--) h2[i] = lh_pop(h1, &n, 1);
            printf("top %d:", K);
            for (int i = 0; i < cnt; i++) printf(" %ld", h2[i]);
            printf("\n");
        } else {                                                    /* median: two heaps */
            int nlo = 0, nhi = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i < total; i++) {
                if (nlo == 0 || merged_v[i] <= h1[0]) lh_push(h1, &nlo, merged_v[i], -1);   /* max-heap low */
                else lh_push(h2, &nhi, merged_v[i], 1);                                     /* min-heap high */
                if (nlo > nhi + 1) lh_push(h2, &nhi, lh_pop(h1, &nlo, -1), 1);
                else if (nhi > nlo) lh_push(h1, &nlo, lh_pop(h2, &nhi, 1), -1);
            }
            if (nlo) printf("median %ld\n", h1[0]);
            else printf("median none\n");
        }
    }
    return 0;
}
```

- **K-way merge with a heap of size k:** the heap always holds the next unread entry of each log, so popping the minimum and pushing that log's successor costs O(log k) per element, O(N log k) in total, versus O(N log N) for sorting everything, and it works on **streams** that don't fit in memory. That's how external merge sort, LSM-tree databases and `heapq.merge` work.
- **The composite comparison key** `(t, log, idx)` makes the merge deterministic and stable.
- **Top-K with a bounded min-heap:** the heap keeps the K largest seen so far, its root is the smallest of them, and anything smaller than the root is discarded. That's O(N log K) time and O(K) space.
- **The running median with two heaps** keeps a max-heap of the lower half and a min-heap of the upper half, balanced so the lower median is always at the max-heap's root.
